doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Return to New York in the late 1960s
title: A Europe tour offer and the Vanguard week with Monk
summary: Ware turns down a European tour with Clifford Jordan and plays the Vanguard with Monk, Blackwell and Rouse.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: while, Clifford Jordan is hooking up a tour of Europe he wants me to go on. He called me from Europe. He left and went over there. He called me, "Many they wanted a brochure on you and he got a string of gigs over here. Told me the price and all that. I wasn't ready for it, so I wouldn't go. I'm still working in New York around this time. Eddie Blackwell came by my house. He stayed right around the corner from me. He said, "Man, Monk wants you to work with us." So, that was a joy, to work with the T again, openly at the Vanguard. So we made that Vanguard gig, Archie Shep -- not Archie, but Archie Shep must be talking about me.

Monk, Blackwell, Charlie Rouse (PHONETIC) and I think that was the last time Charlie worked with T. Thelonius was kind of ill and he was saying things that really hurt Charles' feelings, but we made the weekend -- no, we made that week and then Monk went into the hospital. This was all '68 mostly. And I'm working down at Slugs with different little groups and I worked with Sonny Rollins down at the Vanguard. Al Foster, Al Daley (PHONETIC), myself.
